upstream.name: hoytech/quadrable
upstream.architecture: Header-only C++ sparse binary Merkle tree, compact proofs, sync, copy-on-write LMDB-backed store, MemStore, and quadb CLI.

benchmarkDenominator.total: 55 tracked upstream paths; check.cpp has 34 top-level scenarios, 29 equivHeads subcases, 136 verify checks, and 20 verifyThrow checks; `make -r test` passes all 34 upstream scenarios after shallow submodule initialization
benchmarkDenominator.source: Local cloned upstream inventory of check.cpp, Makefile, include/quadrable headers, docs, and shallow-initialized submodules at commit 4f44437dc9b951a91986ad69e2856938387be614.
benchmarkDenominator.runnerStatus: passed 2026-05-22 with `make -r test` after `sudo -n dnf install -y gcc-c++ lmdb-devel libb2-devel libasan` and `git submodule update --init --depth 1 external/hoytech-cpp external/lmdbxx external/docopt.cpp`; reconfirmed 2026-05-22 after the direct upstream `big proof test` PHP mapping, after the tracked string-key `quadb diff`/`patch` PHP mapping, after the file-backed `quadb root`/`status`/`head`/`head rm` PHP mapping, after the file-backed `quadb exportProof --hex`/`--format=FullKeys`/`--int` PHP mapping, after the file-backed `quadb importProof --hex`/`mergeProof --hex` proof-head persistence mapping, after the file-backed proof-head write/delete/fork replay mapping, after the ordered proof/update event-history mapping for updated-root proof merges after persisted proof-head writes, and after the raw integer proof-backed head update/import mapping. Plain `make test` now gets past missing tooling but this GNU Make environment selects the built-in C++ rule without the repo include flags, so `-r` was used to disable built-in rules while running the upstream test target.
benchmarkDenominator.warning: The upstream C++ runner passes locally, but native PHP parity is still partial. Native PHP tests map upstream-compatible BLAKE2s-256 hashing/key behavior, PHP-native integer key overflow rejection, focused in-memory sparse tree update/get/delete scenarios, raw-key `getMultiRaw`, FullKeys proof transport and partial-tree enumeration, direct upstream `big proof test` semantics over a 1000-key tree and -500..499 string-key getMulti window, iterator windows, composite integer/hash keys, compact proof transport, selected proof import/export, shared empty witnesses, integer proof sizing, range proofs, proof-backed updates, mergeProof, sub-proof/range sub-proof export from imported partial trees, bounded sync proof-fragment transport/import, scan-time and final diff parity, deterministic small/full upstream-shaped sync-fuzz convergence, persisted tracked-node sync-fuzz convergence, cached full proof-tree reuse, tracked node-id behavior, persisted tracked node-store snapshots, memStore-range overlays, the named-head MemStore fork guard, native file-backed `quadb` current-head/detached-head reopen semantics with integer import/export lines, tracked string-key `quadb diff`/`patch` line semantics, upstream-shaped `quadb root`/`status`/`head` output and `head rm` behavior, file-backed `quadb exportProof --hex` for hashed, FullKeys, and raw integer keys, file-backed `quadb importProof --hex`/`mergeProof --hex` proof-head persistence, file-backed proof-head writes/deletes/forks with persisted replay, ordered proof/update replay for updated-root proof merges after persisted proof-head writes, raw integer proof-backed head imports/puts/deletes across reopen, delegated WordPress proofs, large WordPress proof-window reads, and an exact WordPress snapshot root. Remaining parity gaps include broader LMDB persistence internals, raw/composite-key CLI ergonomics beyond the native API, and quadb CLI behavior such as importProof/mergeProof dump output, statistics/output formatting, and garbage collection.
